land.text: the Gezira, the Butana and Meroë: 'Meroë was then taken by the Kingdom of Alodia' (Meroë page)

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Kingdom of Kush'; 'Founded sometime after the ancient Kingdom of Kush fell, around 350 AD'; first mentioned as a kingdom in 569 (infobox 'First mentioned: 6th century'). 347 is Cliopatria's hand-over from Kush.

land.text: Soba and the Gezira: 'In 1504-1505 the Funj founded the Funj sultanate, incorporating Abdallah Jammah's domain'

successors.note: Cliopatria starts the Funj in 1507 and keeps Alodia to 1506; the page's 1504-1505 is used. The Abdallab of Abdallah Jammah held the Soba area as the Funj's partners.

land.text: the mountains of Fazughli in the Ethiopian-Sudanese borderlands, where the Alodian remnant 'gradually retreated ... forming the Kingdom of Fazughli'

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Funj Sultanate, Kingdom of Fazughli, Kingdom of al-Abwab'. Cliopatria lacks Fazughli; it needs a dossier (counterparts_needing_dossiers). Al-Abwab had split off by 1276 (ledger).

capitals.name: Soba
capitals.note: Soba 'was the capital of the Alodian kingdom from the sixth century until around 1500' (Soba page, coordinates 15°31′26″N 32°40′51″E); no earlier seat is known, so the dot stands at Soba from the dossier's start. The city covered about 275 hectares at its height; the kings' residence 'has not yet been identified'.

keyframe_review.note: 347-601, 123,780 km2: the Gezira and the Butana around Soba (bbox 31.1-36.1 E, 15.2-18.3 N), with Meroë inside. The page dates the kingdom's founding 'sometime after ... around 350 AD' and its first mention to 569; converted in 580 under Longinus. Unverified beyond that; no area figure in the infobox (the map caption gives only 'Approximate extent of Alodia in the 10th century').

correction.text: the shape as drawn (the Gezira and the Butana around Soba, Meroë inside); the ledger adds the 10th-century extent from c. 950 (Ibn Hawqal and al-Aswani: Alodia 'more powerful than Makuria, more extensive and having a larger army'; 'the Alodian-controlled Al-Ahdin, which has been identified with the Nuba Mountains'; 'the Eastern Desert along the Red Sea coast'; but not 'Al-Jeblien, which was controlled by Makuria'), takes away al-Abwab in 1276 ('recorded as an independent splinter kingdom') and everything beyond the Soba-Gezira core by 1450 ('By the second half of the 15th century, Arabs had settled in the entire central Sudanese Nile valley' except 'the area around Soba')

keyframe_review.note: 602-1501, one 900-year shape of 123,780 km2: far smaller than the 10th-century description (the Gezira, Butana, Nuba Mountains, Red Sea Hills and the Nile to Abu Hamad together are about 640,000 km2 by the gazetteer with the corrections below). The spec is the shape at 602; the ledger adds the wider extent c. 950 (confidence 1, the date of expansion being unknown), removes al-Abwab in 1276 (confidence 2) and the land beyond the core in 1450 (confidence 1). The regions are wider than the page's words (admin-1 units); soft edges.

correction.text: the shape unchanged except that the Nile reach of al-Abwab, split off by 1276 (ledger), is not Alodian; by then the Soba-Gezira core only (Arabs 'had settled in the entire central Sudanese Nile valley' by the second half of the 15th century, 'the area around Soba, which was all that was left of Alodia's domain'), ending in 1504 rather than 1506: 'the Funj attacked and defeated the kingdom of the Nuba in 1504-1505' and 'In 1504-1505 the Funj founded the Funj sultanate'

keyframe_review.note: 1502-1506: Cliopatria keeps Alodia to 1506 and starts the Funj in 1507. Infobox 'Destroyed: c. 1500'; the Shendi tradition dates Soba's destruction by Abdallah Jammah to 1509 after an attack in 1474; David Reubeni still found 'a Kingdom of Soba on the eastern bank of the Blue Nile' in 1523. The funj-sultanate dossier (af-01-b/c) should start in 1504. Repair pass: the ledger now takes the land beyond the core away in 1450 (loss, confidence 1) so the corrected kingdom returns to this shape; the Cliopatria core (123,780 km2) may be larger than 'the area around Soba' of the page, and reaches the al-Abwab reach north of the Atbara confluence, hence the minus.

region.text: the Gezira and the Butana around Soba, with Meroë

ledger.note: 347: Alwa rises in the Gezira after Kush. 'Founded sometime after the ancient Kingdom of Kush fell, around 350 AD'; a town named Alwa is on the 4th-century Ezana Stone; 'Meroë was then taken by the Kingdom of Alodia' (Meroë page); first mentioned as a kingdom in 569. The year is Cliopatria's hand-over from Kush; Soba is attested as capital from the 6th century. Repair pass: the Soba page says only 'It was the capital of the medieval Nubian kingdom of Alodia from the sixth century until around 1500' and gives no 4th-century date; 347 stays Cliopatria's year at confidence 1.

region.text: the extent Ibn Hawqal (mid-10th century) and al-Aswani describe, without Makuria's 950 land: the Gezira between the White and Blue Niles, the Butana to the Atbara, 'the Alodian-controlled Al-Ahdin, which has been identified with the Nuba Mountains' (South Kordufan), 'the Eastern Desert along the Red Sea coast' and the region of the Gash Delta, and al-Abwab down the Nile to Abu Hamad; not northern Kordofan ('Al-Jeblien, which was controlled by Makuria and probably corresponded with northern Kordofan')

ledger.note: c. 950: Alodia at its widest. 'A century later, in the mid-10th century, Alodia was visited by traveler and historian Ibn Hawqal'; al-Aswani found it 'more powerful than Makuria, more extensive and having a larger army'; Eusebios reigned c. 938-955; 'a vassal king loyal to Alodia governed the region around the Gash Delta' (the Kassala part of the Beja country is therefore a client, not core). The pages do not date the expansion from the Gezira core, so 950 is the year of the description, not of conquest, and the land is taken from nobody (Beja, Nuba and Noba peoples without a Cliopatria row). Repair pass: the Kordofan region (360,130 km2) is replaced by South Kordufan (the Nuba Mountains, 134,796 km2) because the page gives northern Kordofan to Makuria, and the whole is clipped by Cliopatria's Makuria shape of 950 (the unclipped union overlapped it by 76,376 km2), so the makuria dossier needs no matching loss. The corrected extent is about 620,000 km2 (the core included, about 640,000), 5.2 times Cliopatria's 123,780 km2. The 943 overlordship is disputed ('al Masudi wrote that the Makurian king ruled over Alodia, while Ibn Hawqal wrote that it was the other way around'). The Ibn Hawqal page (opened for the thin item) says nothing of Alodia.

region.text: al-Abwab, 'previously described as the northernmost Alodian province', from the Atbara confluence 'downstream to Abu Hamad' ('Abu Hamad likely constituted the northernmost outpost of the Alodian province known as al-Abwab'), outside Makuria's 1275 shape

ledger.note: By 1276: al-Abwab is an independent kingdom. 'By 1276 al-Abwab, previously described as the northernmost Alodian province, was recorded as an independent splinter kingdom' (infobox 'Succeeded by ... Kingdom of al-Abwab'); the year is the page's first record, the split may be earlier. The region (River Nile state without the Shendi-Meroë reach) is the researcher's; kingdom-of-al-abwab needs a dossier. Repair pass: the spec is clipped by Cliopatria's Makuria shape of 1275 (the unclipped River Nile state minus Shendi overlapped it by 50,600 km2). The Al-Abwab page could not be loaded (URL_NOT_FOUND, retried once), so the extent and the end of the kingdom stay unread; the Alodia page adds: 'The precise circumstances of its secession and its relations with Alodia thereafter remain unknown'; 'No evidence for a major Alodian settlement has been discovered north of the confluence of the two Niles'.

region.text: the Sudanese Red Sea state, standing for 'the region between the Red Sea ports of Aydhab and Suakin'

ledger.note: By December 1365: the Red Sea reach is Banu Kanz land (mirror of banu-kanz ledger 3). Banu Kanz page, opened 2026-11-01: the Banu Kanz and Banu Ikrima were 'in control of the region between the Red Sea ports of Aydhab and Suakin'; 'The Kanz al-Dawla and other chiefs surrendered to the Mamluk governor of Qus in December 1365.' The page gives no earlier date and no handover; the Alodia page's 'Eastern Desert along the Red Sea coast' is a 10th-century description (ledger 1). The 1450 loss below then finds the coast already gone. Added fx-25.

region.text: everything the c. 950 gain added outside the Soba-Gezira core and the al-Abwab reach: the Nile valley around the core, the Nuba Mountains and the Beja country; 'By the second half of the 15th century, Arabs had settled in the entire central Sudanese Nile valley' except 'the area around Soba'

ledger.note: By 1450: Alodia shrinks to the Soba-Gezira core. The page gives the end state, not the sequence: 'From the 12th, and especially the 13th century, Alodia was declining'; 'During the 14th and 15th centuries much of what is now Sudan was overrun by Arab tribes' (the first recorded migration 'dates to 1324'); 'It was the disintegration of Makuria in the late 14th century' that opened the way (Adams); the Butana and Gezira 'was the target of those Arabs who had lived among the Beja in the Eastern Desert'; 'By the second half of the 15th century, Arabs had settled in the entire central Sudanese Nile valley' except 'the area around Soba, which was all that was left of Alodia's domain'. 1450 is the start of the second half of the century, the researcher's bridge; the periphery (Nuba Mountains, Eastern Desert, Gash Delta) is undated on the page and is taken at the same date; the land passes to Arab tribes, not to a state (nobody). Reviewer's fix: without this loss the corrected kingdom stayed about 500,000 km2 larger than the 1502 keyframe.

1504: the Funj and Abdallah Jammah end Alwa. 'In 1504-1505 the Funj founded the Funj sultanate, incorporating Abdallah Jammah's domain'; the Tabaqat Dayfallah 'briefly mentions that the Funj attacked and defeated the kingdom of the Nuba in 1504-1505'; the Shendi tradition has Soba 'destroyed by Abdallah Jammah in 1509 having already been attacked in 1474'; infobox 'Destroyed: c. 1500'. A remnant 'gradually retreated to the mountains of Fazughli ... forming the Kingdom of Fazughli', and in 1523 David Reubeni found 'a Kingdom of Soba on the eastern bank of the Blue Nile'.

wars.name: Fall of Alodia (Abdallab and Funj)
wars.outcome: Soba attacked in 1474 and, by the Shendi tradition, 'destroyed by Abdallah Jammah in 1509'; the Funj 'attacked and defeated the kingdom of the Nuba in 1504-1505' and founded their sultanate 'incorporating Abdallah Jammah's domain'. Alodia ends in 1504; a remnant retreats to Fazughli.
wars.note: The Soba page adds nothing on the fall (it says only that the capital lasted 'until around 1500'). The war is dated to 1505 here although the Shendi tradition's 1509 is on the page.

certainty.note: Every frontier approximate: the Makurian frontier near Abu Hamad/al-Abwab, the Kordofan and Red Sea Hills edges and the Ethiopian border ('it is likely that it bordered the Ethiopian highlands') are readings of 10th-century travellers.

notes:
One state. The brief asked whether the 1159-year row is successive states: the Alodia page treats Alwa as one kingdom from after Kush's fall to c. 1500 with one capital, Soba; no split, no new slug. The start is Cliopatria's 347 (page: 'around 350 AD', first mention 569; confidence 1); the end is moved from Cliopatria's 1506 to 1504 (the Funj attack and foundation 1504-1505), so the funj-sultanate dossier should start in 1504, not 1507.

Extent. Cliopatria's single 123,780 km2 shape for 900 years is far smaller than the 10th-century extent the page gives (Gezira, Butana, Nuba Mountains, Red Sea Hills, the Nile to Abu Hamad): the alodia_602 correction and the c. 950 gain (confidence 1; the date of expansion is not on the page) add it with the gazetteer's 'Nilotic Sudan', 'Kordofan' and 'Beja country', all wider than the page's words; a gap-filler with the Ibn Hawqal or al-Aswani texts could tighten them. Al-Abwab is removed from 1276 (its first record as independent).

Counterparts needing dossiers: Kingdom of al-Abwab (kingdom-of-al-abwab; the Atbara-to-Abu Hamad reach, independent by 1276, a Mamluk ally against Makuria in the usual accounts; end unknown on the pages), Kingdom of Fazughli (kingdom-of-fazughli; the Alodian remnant in the Blue Nile borderlands after c. 1500), the Abdallab (abdallab; Abdallah Jammah's domain north of Soba, absorbed into the Funj 1504-1505). Gazetteer names needed: al-Abwab (region), Butana (region: between the Nile and the Atbara), Nuba Mountains/Al-Ahdin (region), Fazughli (place or region), Abu Hamad (place).

Pages silent: no area figure; no date for the expansion beyond the Gezira; the Soba page has nothing on the fall; Moses Georgios (c. 1155-1190) was 'joint ruler of Makuria and Alodia', which neither dossier draws as a union for want of territory data. fx-25 (2026-11-01): the Red Sea hills (Sudanese Red Sea state) pass to banu-kanz in 1365 (ledger), the year the Banu Kanz page first shows them in control; before that the 950 gain stands.
